statements.claim: The cowherds of Vrindavan marvelled that a child of seven had held up a great mountain with one hand.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.2: 'yaḥ sapta-hāyano bālaḥ kareṇaikena līlayā' (a seven-year-old boy, with one hand, playfully [held up the mountain]); pack summary: cowherds wondered how a seven-year-old boy could hold up a great mountain.

statements.claim: Putana, the demon woman, came to Vrindavan in the shape of a nurse, took the child to her breast, and the babe whose eyes were barely open drew out her life.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.3-4: 'tokenāmīlitākṣeṇa pūtanāyā mahaujasaḥ' (by the child with barely opened eyes, of mighty Putana [her life was drawn out]).

statements.claim: A whirlwind snatched him up when he was a year old and carried him high into the sky.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.5: 'eka-hāyana āsīno hriyamāṇo vihāyasā' (one-year-old, seated, carried through the sky).

statements.claim: His mother Yashoda caught him stealing butter and bound him to a heavy grinding mortar.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.6: 'kvacid dhaiyaṅgava-stainye mātrā baddha udūkhale' (once, for butter-theft, bound by his mother to a mortar).

statements.claim: A demon slipped among the calves in the form of a calf; the donkey demon and all his kindred were killed; and Pralamba was thrown down by Balarama.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.7-10: 'vatseṣu vatsa-rūpeṇa praviśantaṃ jighāṃsayā', 'hatvā rāsabha-daiteyaṃ tad-bandhūṃś ca', 'pralambaṃ ghātayitvograṃ balena bala-śālinā'.

statements.claim: The serpent Kaliya, whose venom poisoned the river, was subdued and driven out of the lake by the boy.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.11: 'āśī-viṣatamāhīndraṃ damitvā vimadaṃ hradāt' (the great serpent-king of poisonous venom subdued and dispirited from the lake).

statements.claim: Nanda quieted the cowherds by recalling Garga's prophecy: the child was once born of Vasudeva, takes a body each age, has many names and forms, is the delight of cowherds and cattle, will be their welfare, will stand between them and danger, and is equal to Narayana in qualities; Garga then returned home.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.15-22 (Nanda's speech): 'prāgayaṃ vasudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ', 'bahūni santi nāmāni rūpāṇi ca sutasya te', 'eṣa vaḥ śreya ādhāsyad gopa-gokula-nandanaḥ', 'sādhavo dasyu-pīḍitāḥ', 'nārāyaṇa-samo guṇaiḥ', 'garge ca sva-gṛhaṃ gate' (Garga gone to his own house).

statements.claim: The cowherds' deep affection for the boy was hard to set aside even amid their wonder.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.12: 'dustyajaś cānurāgo 'smin sarveṣāṃ no vrajaukasām' (the love for him, hard to give up, of all us Vraja-dwellers).

statements.claim: Nanda had called Garga to Vrindavan to give the child his name; Garga told Nanda in confidence what he could not say loudly.
statements.evidence: Pack confirms Garga foretold about the child to Nanda and returned home; the naming-ceremony framing is standard traditional background, not contradicted by the pack.

notes: Story follows the Bhagavata turn (Nanda recalls Garga's prophecy) as the tradition_note states; no unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Nanda bathed in the Yamuna at night, alone.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'While Nanda bathed in the Yamuna at night'; BP 10.28.1 context.

statements.claim: A servant of Varuna seized Nanda and carried him to Varuna's abode.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.1: 'taṃ gṛhītvānayad bhṛtyo varuṇasyāsuro 'ntikam' (seizing him, the servant/demon of Varuna brought him near [to Varuna]).

statements.claim: The cowherds, missing Nanda, cried out 'Krishna! Rama!'
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.2: 'cukruśus tam apaśyantaḥ kṛṣṇa rāmeti gopakāḥ' (not seeing him, the cowherds cried 'Krishna! Rama!').

statements.claim: Krishna came at the sound and entered the water, going down to Varuna's court.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.3: 'prāptaṃ vīkṣya hṛṣīkeśaṃ' (seeing Hrishikesha [Krishna] arrived); pack summary: Krishna went to Varuna's abode.

statements.claim: Varuna rose, honored Krishna with offerings and worship, bowed, and spoke words of praise and apology.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.3-7: 'loka-pālaḥ saparyayā' (the world-protector with worship); Varuna's speech: 'namas tubhyaṃ bhagavate brahmaṇe paramātmane' (obeisance to you, the supreme Self), 'ajānatā māmakena mūḍhenākārya-vedinā' (by my fool servant who did not know what was right), 'mamāpy anugrahaṃ kṛṣṇa kartum arhasy aśeṣa-dṛk' (grant me grace, O all-seeing Krishna).

statements.claim: Krishna accepted the honor without anger, and Varuna returned Nanda to him.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'Varuna, honoring him, returned Nanda with apologies.'

statements.claim: Krishna brought his father back up through the water to the bank where the cowherds waited.
statements.evidence: Implied by BP 10.28.1-8 rescue sequence; pack summary: Krishna freed Nanda.

statements.claim: Nanda was silent for a long moment after climbing out, having seen the lord of the waters bow to the boy.
statements.evidence: Connective coda consistent with pack; Nanda's telling is the premise of DKS_0064 (BP 10.28.9).

notes: All event claims match BP 10.28.1-8; Varuna's quoted speech mirrors the Sanskrit verses closely.

statements.claim: Nanda told his kinsmen how the lord of the waters had honored Krishna.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.9: 'nandas tv atīndriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā loka-pāla-mahodayam' (Nanda, having seen the extraordinary majesty of the world-protector [told it]); pack summary.

statements.claim: The cowherds' minds grew eager, wondering if the child was the Lord himself.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.10: 'te cautsukya-dhiyo rājan matvā gopās tam īśvaram' (the cowherds, their minds eager, thinking him the Lord).

statements.claim: Krishna, the all-seeing one, perceived the desire of his people and, being full of mercy, resolved to grant it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.11-13: 'sa bhagavān vijñāyākhila-dṛk svayam', 'iti sañcintya bhagavān mahā-kāruṇiko hariḥ' (the all-seeing Lord perceived; the greatly merciful Hari reflected).

statements.claim: He reflected that people in this world are caught in ignorance, desire, and karma, unable to see the eternal.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.12: 'jano vai loka etasminn avidyā-kāma-karmabhiḥ' (people in this world, by ignorance, desire and karma).

statements.claim: He led the cowherds to the lake of Brahman, let them sink beneath it, and revealed his own abode — the eternal light of Brahman, which is truth, knowledge, and the infinite.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.14-15: 'satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ yad brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam' (the eternal Brahman-light, truth, knowledge, infinite); 'te tu brahma-hradam nītā magnāḥ kṛṣṇena coddhṛtāḥ' (taken to the lake of Brahman, immersed, and raised up by Krishna).

statements.claim: The light was not the light of sun or moon, but the light from which all lights are born, without beginning or end.
statements.evidence: Doctrinal elaboration of 'brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam'; consistent with the pack's eternal-light claim, not asserted verbatim in it.

statements.claim: The cowherds were filled with supreme bliss beyond anything the world could give, and Krishna drew them up again to the bank.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.15-16: 'coddhṛtāḥ' (raised up by Krishna); 'nandādayas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramānanda-nivṛtāḥ' (Nanda and the others, having seen, filled with supreme bliss).

notes: Theological elaboration of the Brahman-light is benign framing, not a factual divergence.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama went into the forest with the women of Vraja in the evening and began to sing, honouring the night as the moon and stars rose.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.19-21: 'govindo rāmaś cādbhuta-vikramaḥ', 'upagīyamānau lalitaṃ strī-janair baddha-sauhṛdaiḥ', 'niśā-mukhaṃ mānayantāv uditoḍupa-tārakam' (honouring the face of night, moon and stars risen).

statements.claim: The song was sweet and slow and auspicious to the mind and ear of every living thing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.20-22: 'lalitaṃ' (sweet/graceful); 'jagatuḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ manaḥ-śravaṇa-maṅgalam' (they sang what was auspicious to the mind and hearing of all beings).

statements.claim: The gopis, listening, went still and forgot themselves, as if entranced.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.23: 'gopyas tad-gītam ākarṇya mūrcchitā nāvidan' (hearing the song the gopis swooned and knew not [themselves]).

statements.claim: The demon Shankhachuda, a servant of Kubera, seized the gopis and carried them off while the brothers sang.
statements.evidence: Pack summary and BP 10.34.24-25: 'evaṃ vikrīḍatoḥ svairaṃ gāyatoḥ sampramatta-vat', 'tan-nāthaṃ pramadā-janaṃ' (the women whose lord was him); excerpt: 'the demon Shankhachuda, servant of Kubera, carried off the women'.

statements.claim: The gopis cried out 'Krishna! Rama!' as they were carried away.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.26: 'krośantaṃ kṛṣṇa rāmeti' (crying 'Krishna! Rama!').

statements.claim: The brothers cried 'Do not fear!', tore up sal-tree trunks as clubs, and plunged after the demon like two lions.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.27: 'mā bhaiṣṭety abhayārāvau śāla-hastau tarasvinau' ('Do not fear' — the two giving fearlessness, sal-trees in hand, impetuous); excerpt: 'pursued him like two lions'.

notes: All details map to BP 10.34.19-27; 'of the kind that had troubled Vrindavan before' is generic connective.

statements.claim: The demon Shankhachuda had carried the gopis off into the forest.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.24-26 (preceding verses in pack's cited range); pack summary for DKS_0065/DKS_0066.

statements.claim: Looking back, the demon saw Krishna and Balarama coming together and perceived them as Time and Death themselves.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.28: 'sa vīkṣya tāv anuprāptau kāla-mṛtyū ivodvijan' (seeing the two arrived, trembling as if [they were] Time and Death).

statements.claim: Krishna ran after him wherever he ran.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.29: 'tam anvadhāvad govindo yatra yatra sa dhāvati' (Govinda ran after him wherever he ran).

statements.claim: Krishna overtook the fleeing demon and, with a single blow of his fist to the head, struck him down and killed him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.30: 'avidūra ivābhyetya śiras tasya durātmanaḥ' (approaching as if near, [struck] the head of that evil one); pack excerpt: 'struck his head with his fist'.

statements.claim: Krishna took the bright jewel from the fallen demon's crest and gave it to his elder brother Balarama, while the women looked on.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.31: 'śaṅkhacūḍaṃ nihatyaivaṃ maṇim ādāya bhāsvaram' (having slain Shankhachuda thus, taking the bright jewel); pack excerpt: 'gave it to his elder brother Balarama while the women looked on'.

statements.claim: The women he had taken were safe and saw the whole exchange.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'while the women looked on'; implied by the rescue of the abducted gopis.

notes: The chase imagery and 'not spoil' commentary are connective; all factual beats are in BP 10.34.28-31.

statements.claim: The demon Arishta came in the shape of a savage bull.
statements.evidence: VP 5.14: 'the demon Arisht́a, disguised as a savage bull'; BP 10.36.1-14.

statements.claim: The Vishnu Purana describes him with the colour of a cloud charged with rain, vast horns, eyes like two fiery suns, tongue licking his lips, erect tail, an enormous hump between his shoulders, low-hanging dewlap, and a face scarred from butting trees; his hooves ploughed up the earth.
statements.evidence: VP 5.14 verbatim: 'colour was that of a cloud charged with rain; he had vast horns, and his eyes were like two fiery suns... his tongue was repeatedly licking his lips; his tail was erect... a hump of enormous dimensions... his dewlap hung low, and his face was marked with scars from butting against the trees... he ploughed up the ground with his hoofs.'

statements.claim: He was a demon who haunted the forests in the shape of a bull, destroying hermits and ascetics.
statements.evidence: VP 5.14: 'the demon who perpetually haunts the forests in the shape of a bull, destroying hermits and ascetics.'

statements.claim: The cows fled in fear, abandoning the herd.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.4: 'paśavo dudruvur bhītā rājan santyajya go-kulam' (the cattle fled in fear, abandoning the herd).

statements.claim: Krishna called the creature out — 'what is this, you lowest of beings, terrifying the cowherds and their animals?' — and slapped his arms together to goad him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.6-7: 'gopālaiḥ paśubhir manda trāsitaiḥ kim asattama' (what is this, O lowest one, the cowherds and animals terrified), 'ity āsphotyācyuto 'riṣṭaṃ tala-śabdena kopayan' (thus slapping his arm, enraging Arishta with the sound).

statements.claim: Arishta pawed the ground, lowered the points of his horns, fixed his reddened eyes on Krishna, and charged.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.8-9: 'khureṇāvanim ullikhan' (pawing the earth with his hoof), 'agra-nyasta-viṣāṇāgraḥ stabdhāsṛg-locano' (horn-points lowered, eyes fixed and bloodshot).

statements.claim: Krishna waited, smiling, for the bull to reach him, then seized him by the horns and flung him a full eighteen paces.
statements.evidence: VP 5.14: 'smiling in sport and derision, awaited the near approach of the bull'; BP 10.36.10: 'gṛhītvā śṛṅgayos taṃ vā aṣṭādaśa padāni' (seizing him by the horns, eighteen paces [he flung him]).

statements.claim: The demon rose and charged again, and Krishna took hold of him by the horns, forced him down, and pressed him to the ground with his foot, killing him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.11-12: 'punar utthāya satvaram', 'sa nigṛhya śṛṅgayoḥ padā samākramya nipātya bhū-tale' (seizing him by the horns, pressing with his foot, throwing him to the ground).

statements.claim: He died vomiting blood, kicking out his feet, his eyes rolling and finding no rest.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.13: 'asṛg vaman mūtra-śakṛt samutsṛjan kṣipaṃś ca pādān anavasthitekṣaṇaḥ' (vomiting blood, excreting urine and dung, kicking his feet, eyes unsteady).

statements.claim: The gods praised Krishna with a shower of flowers, and the herdsmen glorified him as the celestials of old praised Indra over the demon Jambha.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.14: 'stūyamānaḥ dvijātibhiḥ' (praised by the twice-born/gods); pack excerpt: 'the gods praised Krishna with showers of flowers'; VP 5.14: 'the herdsmen glorified Krishńa, as the companies of the celestials of old praised Indra, when he triumphed over the Asura Jambha.'

notes: Story follows the Bhagavata killing method (fling + press down), as its tradition_note declares; the VP horn-tearing variant is not asserted.

statements.claim: Keshi came to Vrindavan in the shape of a horse, sent by Kamsa, who wanted Krishna dead.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (BP): 'sent by Kamsa'; Harivamsha 1.79: 'king Kansa sent an emissary to Keshi for destroying Krishna.'

statements.claim: His mane tossed like a storm-cloud and his neighing was itself a terror.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.1: 'vāla-vighūrṇitāmbudam' (clouds whirled by his mane); Harivamsha 1.79: 'trifle at the wind with his neighing'.

statements.claim: The Harivamsha says he was born along with Kamsa, as dear to the king as his own life, a peerless fighter who had never met his equal.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.79: 'peerless in battle, is born with Kansa, and is his life though ranging outward... the foremost of the sinful.'

statements.claim: He killed the cows and the cowherds and fed on them, and wherever he ranged the forest fell empty: people and cattle withdrew, paths went unused, and animals could no longer travel the forest roads.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.79: 'Killing the cows and cow-herds... began to feed on beef... continually fed on human flesh', 'made the forest empty', 'the Gopas, who derive their sustenance through woods and the kine left it', 'the animals could not wend the forest roads.'

statements.claim: Following the sound of men, the horse came to the settlement of the cowherds; the women, boys and men set up a cry and fled to Krishna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.79: 'following in anger the noise of men... arrived at the settlement of the milk-men', 'the Gopa-women, with their children, and the Gopas, setting up a cry, fled away to their master Krishna.'

statements.claim: Krishna promised them safety and went out to meet the demon, despite cowherds urging him back — 'you are only a boy, and this one is beyond the strength of all.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.79: 'Krishna promised them safety and went out to meet Keshi'; 'thou art a boy and that one of evil ways is beyond the power of all.'

statements.claim: The horse charged with his mouth open as if to drink the sky, eyes and teeth bared, neck raised; Krishna roared like a lion and met the rush.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.1-2: 'upāhvayat sa vyanadan mṛgendra-vat' (he called out roaring like a lion), 'makhena khaṃ pibann ivābhyadravad' (rushing with mouth as if drinking the sky); Harivamsha: 'expanding his eyes and teeth and raising up his neck.'

statements.claim: The horse struck at him with his fore-hooves, and Krishna slipped aside, caught hold of him, whirled him around, and hurled him to the ground.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.2-3: 'jaghāna padbhyām' (he struck with his feet); 'tad vañcayitvā tam adhokṣajo ruṣā pragṛhya dorbhyāṃ parividhya pādayoḥ' (having deceived him, seized him with his arms, whirled him by the feet).

statements.claim: Keshi rose again, angrier than before, and came at him with jaws stretched open to bite; Krishna, smiling, thrust his arm into the open mouth, like a hand thrust down a serpent's hole.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.4: 'labdha-saṃjñaḥ punar utthito ruṣā vyādāya keśī tarasāpatad harim', 'so 'py asya vaktre bhujam uttaraṃ smayan praveśayām āsa yathoragaṃ bile' (smiling, he put his arm into his mouth as into a serpent's hole).

statements.claim: The demon's teeth met the arm and dropped out as though they had touched hot iron, and the arm swelled until it filled the creature and stopped his breath; Keshi choked, kicked, and fell dead.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.5-6: 'dantā nipetur... tapta-maya-spṛśo yathā' (teeth fell as if touching molten metal), 'bāhuś ca tad-deha-gato... saṃvavṛdhe' (the arm within the body grew), 'niruddha-vāyuś caraṇāṃś ca vikṣipan' (breath stopped, kicking his feet).

statements.claim: His body split open like a ripened gourd — one source says torn asunder like a tree struck by lightning — and Krishna drew his arm out.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.7: 'tad-dehataḥ karkaṭikā-phalopamād vyasor apākṛṣya bhujaṃ mahā-bhujaḥ' (withdrawing his arm from the body like a karkaṭikā fruit); VP 5.16: 'fell down, torn asunder like a tree struck by lightning.'

statements.claim: The gods showered flowers upon him, and because he had slain Keshi the world would call him Keshava.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (BP): 'the gods showered flowers on Krishna'; Harivamsha 1.79: 'Since thou hast slain Keshi, thou shalt pass by the name of Keshava'; VP 5.16: 'thou shalt be known in the world by the name of Keśava.'

notes: Blends BP, Harivamsha and VP as the pack does; every cited detail (born with Kamsa, empty forest, serpent-hole simile, Keshava name) is in the pack.

statements.claim: The boys of Vrindavan played a game on the slopes of the hill where the herd grazed, some as keepers of the calves and some as thieves.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.25-26: 'te paśūn pālāś cārayanto 'dri-sānuṣu' (herding cattle on mountain slopes), 'tatrāsan katicic corāḥ pālāś ca katicin' (some there were thieves, some keepers).

statements.claim: Vyoma, the son of Maya, a demon and master of deception, dressed as a cowherd boy and was taken for one of the boys.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.27: 'maya-putro mahā-māyo vyomo gopāla-veṣa-dhṛk' (Vyoma, son of Maya, of great illusion, wearing a cowherd's garb).

statements.claim: One by one he led boys away and sealed them in a cave in the mountain, so the game went on around the empty places where they had been.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.28: 'giri-daryāṃ vinikṣipya nītaṃ nītaṃ mahāsuraḥ' (sealing them in a mountain cave, the great demon carried them away one by one).

statements.claim: Krishna, whom the verses call the giver of refuge to the good, saw what was happening and understood at once.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.29: 'tasya tat karma vijñāya kṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇa-daḥ satām' (Krishna, the refuge-giver to the good, knowing that deed).

statements.claim: Krishna left off the shape and size of a boy and stood in his own form, vast and strong as a king among mountains.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.30: 'sa nijaṃ rūpam āsthāya girīndra-sadṛśaṃ balī' (assuming his own form, mighty, like a king of mountains).

statements.claim: He seized Vyoma with both hands, threw him down upon the earth, and ended him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.31: 'taṃ nigṛhyācyuto dorbhyāṃ pātayitvā mahī-tale' (seizing him with his arms, throwing him on the ground).

statements.claim: Krishna broke through the covering that sealed the cave and brought the boys out, one after another, into the light.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.32: 'guhā-pidhānaṃ nirbhidya gopān niḥsārya kṛcchrataḥ' (breaking the cave's covering, bringing the cowherds out with difficulty).

notes: Every claim maps to BP 10.37.24-32; 'the mountain gave back everyone it had taken' is connective coda.
